## Cost analysis

Current best `nocrop_deep_einsum_cp7_qreuse_vec_fast` cost = **283** = memory 0 + params 283. It keeps the graph input and output free, uses one static-shape output Einsum, and pays only reusable factor initializers:

| tensor | shape | dtype | bytes | note |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| `Q` | `[30,7]` | F32 init | 210 params | output-position factors for 3 low, 3 high, 1 all-ones CP components; also reused for input source selection |
| `C` / `P` | two `[3,7]` | F32 init | 42 params | basis-to-component and source-coordinate component factors; reused to expose Q's low columns |
| `D` / `X` | two `[4,3]` | F32 init | 24 params | tied direct selector and signed swapped selector |
| `Lambda` | `[4]` | F32 init | 4 params | term weights `[1,1,0.5,-0.5]` |
| `G` | `[3]` | F32 init | 3 params | selects the low row of `C/P/Q` for the source-crop replacement |

Params = `Q` 210 + `C/P` 42 + `D/X` 24 + `Lambda` 4 + `G` 3 = 283. The prior cost-370 CP7 graph paid `A[30,3]` (90 params) to select the input source rows/cols. This version reconstructs the same source selector in-kernel as `sum_m,a Q[axis,m] * C[a,m] * P[src,m] * G[a]`, where `G=[1,0,0]` keeps only Q's low one-hot columns. No `A` tensor or materialized view is needed, and all added products remain inside the final output Einsum. The output is the only node output, so memory is 0; full real-input profile agrees (`static=283 profile=283` with `--arcgen 266`).

Superseded safe fallbacks: `nocrop_deep_einsum_cp7_fast` cost = 370, SHA256 `1b0daca6d60d197df5394545d99a1b34362eaa89903506a3fe1dd50cf145fe18`, fully byte-equal; `nocrop_deep_einsum` cost = 408, SHA256 `fb478d7e75475ea7ec6f9c6993a3ca944eb4240d28734ba51566fa135425bdca`, fully byte-equal; `gatherpad_quad_nopadval` cost = 513, SHA256 `f397582cac0e61f8156a4e603a325217faf98347c95cf6ed040b6ff3d15458e9`, fully byte-equal. No absolute floor is claimed: a further exact formulation probably must factor or eliminate `Q[30,7]` itself, since the output still needs three low positions, three high positions, and one neutral all-ones mode across both axes.

## Don't-do log

- `freeout_quad` Equal-last: cost 1,092; pays `[1,1,30,30]` uint8 padded canvas before free Equal.
- `boolpad_quad`: cost 552; moves Pad after Equal but keeps transpose/slice/concat quadrant assembly.
- `gatherpad_quad` without Pad-18 axes: cost 516; same graph, superseded by axes trim to 514.
- `gatherpad_quad` with explicit `false` Pad value: cost 514; superseded by omitting the optional value input (cost 513).
- `gatherpad_quad_nopadval`: cost 513; safe full-gated fallback, superseded by no-crop deep Einsum at 408 and then CP7-fast at 370.
- Single `bchw,hH,wW` einsum-final as in task142: not expressive for D4 swapped-axis quadrants without adding a second charged transpose/crop path or non-separable maps.
- `nooh6_deep_einsum` crop variant: final free-output Einsum avoids `oh6` and passes visible 266/266, but costs 684 = crop 360 + params 324; superseded by folding the source crop into `A[30,3]` selector operands.
- Prompt-order no-crop deep Einsum: same 408 static cost and correct, but ~4.228 ms/run local timing was too slow-risky for full gates; operand reordering made full gates complete.
- `sreuse`: cost 396 by reusing identical `S_hH/S_wW`; visible clean, superseded by signed tied selectors.
- `signedtie_fast`: cost 388 by tying the direct selector and representing swapped low/high off-diagonal with signed weights; visible/profile/truth-2k clean, superseded by CP7 M factorization.
- `cp7`/`cp7_preselect`: costs 370/381 and correct, but initial D,D,X,X operand order was slow (~30s per 2k truth); fast H-side-before-W-side order fixed runtime and made `cp7_fast` full-gateable.
- `qreuse_fast`: cost 301 by replacing `A[30,3]` with an explicit `L[3,7]` low-column selector over `Q`; visible 266/266, superseded by `qreuse_vec_fast` at 283 using only `G[3]`.
- One-node depthwise Conv/ConvTranspose-as-output: 8x8 offset box duplicates to 640 params across 10 channels before correctness, and desired/undesired offset conflicts leak outside the 6x6 active output.
- Row-code/column-code BitwiseAnd final: exact with 6 column bits in principle, but dynamic `[1,10,30,1]` row codes require a charged row-code surface plus extraction chain above the Pad-last rung.
- 10-channel crop/mirror throughout: F32 one-hot intermediates dominate the u8 color-index route.
